7:It then tests its suspicion: it replays the weakest setup's real past tasks under candidate setups, each task at the commit before it with no future history. It promotes a candidate only if nothing regresses, and opens a pull request with the change. Finally it books the team's AI workforce into its [cfo.ai](https://cfo.ai) plan. Every Roster run is traced in [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com).
8-
9-This file is the engineering contract for everyone building Roster, humans and agents. Keep to its names and shapes. If you need to change a shared shape, change `src/types.ts` minimally and say so in your PR.
10-
11----
12-
13-## Overview: the loop
14-
15-```
16-repo URL
17- → Ingest   Entire checkpoints → sessions (setup, model, tokens, prompts, files, commit)
18- → Score    survival · reverted · rework (human/agent) · unattended · cost            evidence level A (observational)
19- → Review   difficulty-matched scorecard → "suspect: setup X" (Mantel–Haenszel OR, CI, p)
20- → Plan     coordinator: stratified task sample, candidates, budget, stop rules
21- → Replay   each task at its parent commit in an isolated sandbox; incumbent + candidates
22- → Grade    hidden acceptance tests · suite at parent · scope guard · blind diff-judge · reruns
23- → Gate     promote only if nothing regresses                                         evidence level B (controlled replay)
24-     └ reject → Candidates: a new rules file from the failure taxonomy → Replay
25- → Act      pull request: setups/<id>.json + rules file + evidence
26- → Forward  pre-registered new tasks, paired old vs new, blind grading                evidence level C (forward)
27- → Book     cfo.ai: AI Workforce department + hire-vs-scale scenario, read back to verify
28-```
29-
30-The rule: a setup is never called "worse" on level A alone. Every page prints the evidence level next to every claim.
31-
32-## Setups
33-
34-**Setup** = `harness` + `model` + `rules_hash` (+ `plugins_hash` when recorded).
35-
36-| Part | Where it comes from |
37-|---|---|
38-| `harness` | Entire metadata |
39-| `model` | The **resolved** model the run reports (e.g. `modelUsage`), never the requested flag |
40-| `rules_hash` | sha256 of the rules file in effect at the session's parent commit, normalised (LF line endings, trimmed): `CLAUDE.md` for Claude Code, `AGENTS.md` for Codex, `.cursor/rules/*` / `.cursorrules` for Cursor. It also covers any appended system prompt the session records. If unknown, `null`; never a guess |
41-
42-### The four setups building this repo
43-These live in `setups/`:
44-
45-| Id | Harness | Model | Rules |
46-|---|---|---|---|
47-| A | Claude Code | Opus 5.5 | `setups/rules/default.md` |
--
56:3. **One task per worktree.** One task gets one worktree and one branch, launched by `scripts/run-setup.sh <setup> <task>` with isolated settings: `--setting-sources project --strict-mcp-config`. The project `.mcp.json` holds only Entire and neatlogs.
57-4. **Merging.** Merge with `git merge --no-ff`. **Never squash**: squashing drops the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers that attribution depends on.
58-5. **Commit prefixes.** Human fixes are separate commits prefixed `human:`. Operational work is prefixed `ops:` and excluded from every experiment.
59-
60-## Entire checkpoint format
61-
62-This section was verified on 2026-10-10 against 6 public repos (2,421 session rows). Redacted real samples are in `tests/fixtures/samples/`. Build against them.
63-
64-### Two storage backends (read both)
65-
66-| Backend | Where | Layout | Checkpoint id |
67-|---|---|---|---|
68-| `branch` (legacy, visible on GitHub) | `refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1`, one cumulative tree | `<id[0:2]>/<id[2:]>/…` | 12 hex chars, e.g. `02674b7ab946` → `02/674b7ab946/` |
69-| `git-refs` (default since CLI 0.10) | One ref per checkpoint: `refs/entire/checkpoints/<id[-2:]>/<id>` | The ref commit's tree root is the checkpoint | 26-char ULID (12-hex ids also occur) |
70-
71-- An empty `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch means the repo migrated to refs, so always try both backends.
72-- On refs, the ref commit's message carries the trailers `Checkpoint: <id>`, `Entire-Session: <uuid>`, `Entire-Strategy: manual-commit|import` and `Entire-Agent: <name>`.
73-- Commits on code branches link to a checkpoint with the trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>`.
74-
75-### The tree of one checkpoint
76-
77-```
78-metadata.json                 checkpoint root: cli_version, checkpoint_id, strategy, branch, files_touched, sessions[], token_usage
79-<n>/metadata.json             one per session in this checkpoint (n = 0, 1, …)
80-<n>/full.jsonl                the agent's native transcript (best-effort redacted)
81-<n>/transcript.jsonl          Entire's compact transcript (CLI ≥ 0.10)
82-<n>/prompt.txt                user prompts joined by "\n\n---\n\n" (sometimes missing)
83-<n>/content_hash.txt          "sha256:<hex>" of full.jsonl
84-tasks/<tool_use_id>/          subagents: task.json, agent-<id>.jsonl
85-```
86-
87-- Paths in the root `sessions[]` are repo-absolute on the branch backend (`/02/674b7ab946/0/metadata.json`). Normalise them.
88-
89-### Session `metadata.json`: the keys we use
90-
91-| Key | Notes |
92-|---|---|
93-| `session_id` | The agent's own id. **The same session recurs across checkpoints.** Aggregate per session over all its checkpoints |
94-| `agent` | Display name: `Claude Code`, `Codex`, `Copilot CLI`, `Factory AI Droid`, `Pi`, … |
95-| `model` | Often `""`. Fall back to the transcript (below) |
96-| `created_at` | RFC3339; roughly the commit time |
--
246:- **On our own repo:** a PR with `setups/<id>.json`, the rules file, the review summary, an evidence table, neatlogs trace links and entire.io links.
247-- **On other people's repos:** never unsolicited. Only for teams that opted in.
248-
249:### Observability (neatlogs)
250-- **Trace structure:** a `WORKFLOW review` root, then `AGENT coordinator`, then `TOOL` spans (one per ingest, score, replay attempt, grade and cfo.ai write), plus a `GUARDRAIL gate` span.
251-- **Attributes:** `roster.setup, roster.task, roster.attempt, roster.failure_code, roster.evidence_level, roster.repo, roster.cost_usd`.
252-- **Session:** `identify(session_id = review_id)`.
253-- **Detections:**
254-
255-| Detection | Fires when |
256-|---|---|
257-| D1 silent pass | The visible suite passed, but hidden acceptance or the scope guard failed |
258-| D2 low attribution confidence | More than 30% of a setup's lines are unmapped |
259-| D3 cost anomaly | Cost exceeds 3× the incumbent median |
260-| D4 environment flake | F6 hits the same task across ≥ 2 setups |
261-
262:- **No API key:** with `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` unset, observability is a no-op with one warning.
263-
264-### Book (cfo.ai)
265-- **Writes over the cfo.ai MCP:**
266-  - an **AI Workforce** department: monthly spend per setup, surviving changes, cost per surviving change, unattended %
267-  - a **Hire 1 engineer vs scale the promoted setup** scenario
268-- **Verify:** read the blocks back and diff them against `book.json`. A mismatch means retry once, then report it.
269-
270-### Forward run (pre-registered)
271-- **Registration:** the backlog (`experiments/forward-backlog.md`) and its acceptance tests (`experiments/acceptance/`) are committed, and their sha256 is published, **before** the review that picks the setups.
272-- **The acceptance tests** are written by a separate agent from the task text alone, before either setup runs.
273-- **Each task runs through both setups** in paired worktrees from the same main commit.
274-- **Grading is blind** (random X/Y labels).
275-- **Merge policy:** pass beats fail. If both pass, the blind judge's preference wins. If the judge ties, a random pick with a logged seed. Merge with `--no-ff`.
276-- **Statistics:** McNemar exact (two-sided, α = 0.05) on the pairs, and Wilcoxon signed-rank on cost.
277-- **Stop rule:** after ≥ 15 pairs, if the promoted setup has lost at least 3 more discordant pairs than it has won, open a revert PR and continue on the old setup.
278-- **Invalidated tasks** are excluded for both setups, with a reason.
279-

result.output:
I can't reproduce the full page verbatim, but here is a summary of the TypeScript SDK content. The page describes itself as "Install, initialize, and instrument TypeScript/Node.js LLM and agent apps with Neatlogs."

**Package and install**
- npm package: `neatlogs`
- Install with `npm install neatlogs@latest`
- Requires Node.js `>=18`. CI baselines are Node 18, 20, and 22.

**Initialization**
`init()` is async, so call it with `await`. Wrap your client with the matching `wrap*` helper. The page's example uses `wrapOpenAI`:

```ts
await init({ apiKey: process.env.NEATLOGS_API_KEY, workflowName: 'my-first-app' });
const client = wrapOpenAI(new OpenAI());
```

For EU projects, pass `endpoint: 'https://eu.ingest.neatlogs.com'` (base URL only).

Documented `init()` options: `apiKey`, `workflowName`, `tags`, `userId`, `metadata`, `captureLogs`, `sampleRate`, `mask`, `pii`/`piiSpanTypes`, `endpoint`, `batchSize` (default 100), `flushInterval` (default 5 seconds), `tracerProvider`, `registerShutdownHandlers`, and `debug`.

**Creating spans**
- `span({ kind, name?, ... }, fn)` wraps a function and returns an instrumented version with the same signature.
- Span kinds include `WORKFLOW` (top-level entry point), `AGENT` (reasoning step that calls an LLM), `TOOL` (a function the agent calls), and `GUARDRAIL` (a safety or validation check). The page does not list attributes specific to `GUARDRAIL`.
- `SpanOptions` include `name`, `captureInput`/`captureOutput`, `role`, `goal`, `toolName`, `parameters`, `model`, `dimension`, and `mask`.
- `@Span(...)` works as a decorator on class methods, with TypeScript 5.0+ and `experimentalDecorators: false`.
- `trace({ name, kind }, async (activeSpan) => ...)` runs an inline block. Use `activeSpan.setAttribute(...)` to set attributes.
- `setTraceOutput(value)` sets the trace's displayed output.
- `PromptTemplate` and `UserPromptTemplate` support `{{variable}}` placeholders and are passed to `trace()`.
- `log()` records timestamped steps when `captureLogs: true`.

**Lifecycle**
- `await flush()` exports buffered data.
- `await shutdown()` drains and shuts down.
- `flushAll()` drains all registered Neatlogs clients.
- Scripts should await both in `finally`. Long-running servers should call them once on shutdown, not per request.

**Supported libraries**
The page's table includes `wrapClaudeAgentSDK(sdk)`, importable from `neatlogs` or `neatlogs/claude-agent-sdk`, for SDKs that expose the documented `query()` API. The page has no usage code for it.

**Not covered on this page**
- The page has no identify/session API reference. It mentions `identify()` only in passing, and refers readers to the End-User Identity page.
- There is no trace URL helper.
- There is no `wrapClaudeAgentSDK` code example.
